question: Under MCL 339.2512d(1), a licensee acting under the terms of a service provision agreement shall perform the duties described in which subsection?
choice_a: Subsection (4)
choice_b: Subsection (5)
choice_c: Subsection (2)
choice_d: Subsection (3) only, not subsection (2)
explanation: Sec. 2512d(1) requires a licensee under a service provision agreement to perform the duties described in subsection (2).

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(1), may a real estate broker authorize a designated agent to represent the client?
choice_a: No, designated agency is prohibited under a service provision agreement
choice_b: Yes, and the authorization may be oral if witnessed
choice_c: Yes, but only for buyer agency agreements, never listing agreements
choice_d: Yes, but only if that authorization is in writing
explanation: A real estate broker may authorize a designated agent to represent the client, if that authorization is in writing.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(a), what standard must a licensee exercise in representing a client under a service provision agreement?
choice_a: Reasonable care and skill in representing the client and carrying out the responsibilities of the agency relationship
choice_b: The highest possible standard of care regardless of circumstances
choice_c: No specific standard; only good faith is required
choice_d: The standard applicable to attorneys under the Michigan Rules of Professional Conduct
explanation: Subsection (2)(a) requires the exercise of reasonable care and skill in representing the client and carrying out the responsibilities of the agency relationship.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(b), which minimum duty requires a licensee to carry out what was actually agreed to?
choice_a: The performance of any oral promises made during negotiations
choice_b: The performance of the terms of the service provision agreement
choice_c: The performance of industry-standard MLS practices regardless of the agreement
choice_d: The performance of the client's verbal instructions only
explanation: Subsection (2)(b) lists performance of the terms of the service provision agreement as a minimum duty.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(c), a licensee acting under a service provision agreement owes the client which minimum duty?
choice_a: Loyalty to the interest of the brokerage firm above the client
choice_b: Loyalty to whichever party pays the commission
choice_c: Loyalty to the interest of the client
choice_d: Loyalty is not a listed statutory duty
explanation: Subsection (2)(c) lists loyalty to the interest of the client as a minimum duty.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(d), a licensee's compliance duty extends to which laws?
choice_a: Only Michigan real estate licensing statutes
choice_b: Only the licensee's local MLS rules
choice_c: Only federal fair housing law
choice_d: The laws, rules, and regulations of Michigan and any applicable federal statutes or regulations
explanation: Subsection (2)(d) requires compliance with the laws, rules, and regulations of this state and any applicable federal statutes or regulations.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(e), when must a licensee refer the client to other licensed professionals?
choice_a: For expert advice related to material matters that are not within the expertise of the broker
choice_b: Only when the client explicitly demands a referral in writing
choice_c: Never; the licensee must handle all matters personally
choice_d: Only for matters involving property tax appeals
explanation: Subsection (2)(e) requires referral of the client to other licensed professionals for expert advice on material matters outside the broker's expertise.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(f), what must a licensee provide regarding money and property received in which the client has or may have an interest?
choice_a: An accounting only at closing
choice_b: An accounting in a timely manner
choice_c: An accounting only if requested in writing by the client
choice_d: No accounting is statutorily required
explanation: Subsection (2)(f) requires an accounting in a timely manner of all money and property received by the broker in which the client has or may have an interest.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(g), a licensee's confidentiality duty covers what information?
choice_a: Only information the client marks 'confidential' in writing
choice_b: Only financial information, not personal information
choice_c: All information obtained in the course of the agency relationship, unless disclosed with the client's permission or as provided by law
choice_d: Information obtained before the agency relationship began, but not after
explanation: Subsection (2)(g) requires confidentiality of all information obtained in the course of the agency relationship, unless disclosed with the client's permission or as provided by law.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(g), the confidentiality duty specifically includes the duty not to disclose confidential information to whom?
choice_a: Any licensee, including the client's own agent
choice_b: The client's attorney
choice_c: The title insurance company handling closing
choice_d: Any licensee who is not an agent of the client
explanation: Subsection (2)(g) specifically includes the duty not to disclose confidential information to any licensee who is not an agent of the client.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(2), which of the following is NOT listed as a minimum duty a licensee owes a client under a service provision agreement?
choice_a: Guaranteeing the client a minimum sale price
choice_b: The exercise of reasonable care and skill
choice_c: Loyalty to the interest of the client
choice_d: Confidentiality of information obtained in the agency relationship
explanation: Guaranteeing a minimum sale price is not among the subsection (2) duties (reasonable care/skill, performance of the agreement's terms, loyalty, compliance, referral, accounting, and confidentiality).

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(3)(e), the closing-statement furnishing duty does not apply if the closing is conducted by a title insurance company or by whom else?
choice_a: Any attorney representing either party
choice_b: A person designated to act as the agent of a title insurance company that is licensed or authorized to do business in this state
choice_c: The listing broker's principal broker
choice_d: Any bank providing purchase-money financing
explanation: The exception applies both to a title insurance company and to a person designated to act as its agent, if licensed or authorized to do business in Michigan.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(4), beyond the 'for sale by owner' prohibition, what else does the statute prohibit a licensee representing a seller from doing?
choice_a: Advertising the property using professional photography
choice_b: Disclosing the listing price to other licensees
choice_c: Otherwise misleading the public to believe that the seller is not represented by a real estate broker
choice_d: Marketing the property on more than one website
explanation: Subsection (4) prohibits both 'for sale by owner' advertising and otherwise misleading the public into believing the seller is unrepresented.

question: MCL 339.2512d, governing service provision agreement duties and services, was added to the Occupational Code effective when, and later amended by what act?
choice_a: Added by 1980 Act 299 with no subsequent amendments
choice_b: Added by 2024 Act 122, effective July 25, 2024
choice_c: Added by 2000 Act 236, effective June 27, 2000
choice_d: Added by 2008 Act 90, effective July 1, 2008, and amended by 2016 Act 502, effective March 29, 2017
explanation: Section 2512d was added by 2008 Act 90 (eff. July 1, 2008) and amended by 2016 Act 502 (eff. March 29, 2017).

question: Under MCL 339.2512g(1)(b), a right-to-list home sale agreement is void and unenforceable if it is not signed by whom?
choice_a: All persons that have an ownership interest in the residential real estate considered in the agreement
choice_b: Only the primary titleholder, regardless of co-owners
choice_c: A notary public
choice_d: The listing broker's supervising broker
explanation: Subsection (1)(b) voids an agreement not signed by all persons with an ownership interest in the residential real estate at issue.

question: A married couple co-owns a home. The husband alone signs a right-to-list home sale agreement with a broker; the wife, also a titled owner, never signs. Under MCL 339.2512g(1)(b), what is the legal effect?
choice_a: The agreement is fully enforceable against both owners
choice_b: The agreement is void and unenforceable because not all owners signed
choice_c: The agreement binds only the husband's share of the property
choice_d: The agreement becomes valid automatically after 30 days
explanation: Because a co-owner with an ownership interest did not sign, the agreement is void and unenforceable under subsection (1)(b).

question: A right-to-list home sale agreement includes a termination option capped at the initial consideration plus 6% annual interest, but does not conspicuously state the agreement's term and termination option on the first page. Under MCL 339.2512g(1)(d), is the agreement enforceable?
choice_a: Yes, because the termination option cap is the only requirement
choice_b: Yes, because first-page disclosure is only a recommended best practice
choice_c: No, because subdivision (d) requires both the capped termination option AND the conspicuous first-page disclosure
choice_d: No, but only because the term exceeds 2 years
explanation: Subsection (1)(d) requires both the capped termination option under (d)(i) and the conspicuous first-page disclosure under (d)(ii); missing either voids the agreement.

question: MCL 339.2512g, which voids noncompliant right-to-list home sale agreements, was added to the Occupational Code by what act, and when did it take immediate effect?
choice_a: 2016 Act 502, effective March 29, 2017
choice_b: 2008 Act 90, effective July 1, 2008
choice_c: 1980 Act 299, effective October 21, 1980
choice_d: 2024 Act 122, immediate effect July 25, 2024
explanation: Section 2512g was added by 2024 Act 122, with immediate effect on July 25, 2024.

question: A right-to-list home sale agreement was signed on June 1, 2024 and was never extended or renewed. Given that 2024 Act 122 took immediate effect July 25, 2024, does MCL 339.2512g's voidability framework apply to this agreement?
choice_a: No, because the agreement was entered into before the amendatory act's effective date and was not extended or renewed after it
choice_b: Yes, because the statute applies retroactively to all agreements regardless of signing date
choice_c: Yes, but only if the agreement exceeds 2 years
choice_d: No agreement signed in 2024 is ever covered by section 2512g
explanation: Subsection (2) limits application to agreements entered into, extended, or renewed on or after the amendatory act's effective date; this agreement predates that date and was never extended or renewed.

question: A broker pays a homeowner $2,000 initial consideration for a right-to-list home sale agreement. Two years later the owner exercises the termination option. Under MCL 339.2512g(1)(d)(i), what is the maximum consideration the owner may be required to pay to terminate?
choice_a: $2,000 flat, with no interest permitted
choice_b: $2,000 plus interest accruing at 6% per year from the date the initial consideration was paid through the termination date
choice_c: $2,000 plus a statutory penalty of 10%
choice_d: There is no maximum; the broker may set any termination fee
explanation: The termination-option consideration cannot exceed the initial consideration paid, plus interest at 6% per annum running from the payment date through the termination date.

question: Under MCL 339.2501(j), a 'limited service agreement' is defined as what?
choice_a: Any oral agreement to reduce a broker's commission rate
choice_b: A right-to-list home sale agreement lasting less than 1 year
choice_c: A written service provision agreement by which a broker and client establish an agency relationship in which certain services under section 2512d(3)(b), (c), and (d) are knowingly waived in whole or part by the client
choice_d: An agreement that waives all duties under section 2512d(2)
explanation: MCL 339.2501(j) defines a limited service agreement as a written service provision agreement knowingly waiving, in whole or part, the 2512d(3)(b), (c), and (d) services.

question: A seller signs a listing agreement and knowingly waives the licensee's duty to assist with negotiating offers under 2512d(3)(c), while all subsection (2) duties (loyalty, confidentiality, etc.) remain fully in effect. What has the seller signed?
choice_a: A right-to-list home sale agreement
choice_b: An unenforceable agreement, since subsection (2) duties cannot coexist with any waiver
choice_c: A designated agency agreement
choice_d: A limited service agreement
explanation: A service provision agreement knowingly waiving one or more of the 2512d(3)(b), (c), or (d) services is, by definition, a limited service agreement; subsection (2) duties are unaffected.

question: Under MCL 339.2501(w), a right-to-list home sale agreement obligates the owner to do what?
choice_a: List the residential real estate for sale with the real estate broker at a future date, in exchange for consideration
choice_b: Immediately list the property upon signing, with no future-date component
choice_c: Sell the property directly to the broker
choice_d: Pay the broker a commission regardless of whether a listing ever occurs
explanation: A right-to-list home sale agreement obligates the owner to list the residential real estate for sale with the broker at a future date, in exchange for consideration.

question: Under MCL 339.2501(w), what must the broker provide to the owner in exchange for the future right to list?
choice_a: Nothing; the agreement is gratuitous by definition
choice_b: Consideration
choice_c: A completed appraisal report
choice_d: A signed listing agreement executed simultaneously
explanation: The owner's future listing obligation is given in exchange for consideration from the broker.

question: Under MCL 339.2501(w), does the definition of 'right-to-list home sale agreement' include a service provision agreement?
choice_a: Yes, a right-to-list home sale agreement is simply a type of service provision agreement
choice_b: Yes, but only when the broker is representing a seller
choice_c: No; the definition expressly states that a right-to-list home sale agreement does not include a service provision agreement
choice_d: The statute is silent on the relationship between the two terms
explanation: MCL 339.2501(w) expressly excludes a service provision agreement from the definition of a right-to-list home sale agreement.

question: Under MCL 339.2501(x), a 'service provision agreement' is defined as what?
choice_a: Any written contract between a broker and a title company
choice_b: A right-to-list home sale agreement executed more than 2 years before closing
choice_c: An agreement that only a real estate salesperson, not a broker, may execute
choice_d: A buyer agency agreement or listing agreement that is executed by a real estate broker and a client and establishes an agency relationship
explanation: MCL 339.2501(x) defines a service provision agreement as a buyer agency agreement or listing agreement executed by a broker and client that establishes an agency relationship.

question: A homeowner signs an agreement today granting a broker the exclusive right to list her home for sale beginning 18 months from now, in exchange for $1,500 paid at signing. Which statute's voidability requirements govern this agreement?
choice_a: MCL 339.2512g, because this is a right-to-list home sale agreement, not a present listing agreement
choice_b: MCL 339.2512d, because it is a service provision agreement
choice_c: Neither statute applies since no listing has yet occurred
choice_d: MCL 339.2517, because it concerns agency relationship disclosure
explanation: An agreement obligating the owner to list at a future date in exchange for consideration is a right-to-list home sale agreement under 2501(w), governed by 2512g's voidability rules, not the service-provision-agreement rules of 2512d.

question: A right-to-list home sale agreement covering a co-owned home is made orally and signed only by one of the two owners. Under MCL 339.2512g(1), is the agreement enforceable?
choice_a: Yes, because an oral agreement signed by at least one owner satisfies the statute
choice_b: No; it is void and unenforceable on two independent grounds -- it is not in writing and not signed by all owners
choice_c: No, but only because it is oral; the missing signature is not itself disqualifying
choice_d: Yes, as long as the term does not exceed 2 years
explanation: Both the writing requirement of (1)(a) and the all-owners-signed requirement of (1)(b) are independently violated, each of which alone voids the agreement.

question: A licensee's client asks a complex tax-basis question about the sale proceeds that falls outside the licensee's real estate expertise. Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(e), what is the licensee's minimum duty?
choice_a: Provide a best-guess answer to keep the transaction moving
choice_b: Ignore the question since it is outside the scope of the service provision agreement
choice_c: Refer the client to another licensed professional, such as an accountant or attorney, for expert advice on that material matter
choice_d: Refer the client only to another real estate licensee at the same brokerage
explanation: Subsection (2)(e) requires referral of the client to other licensed professionals for expert advice on material matters outside the broker's expertise.

question: A listing agent tells a licensee from a competing brokerage -- who does not represent the seller -- that the seller is desperate to sell quickly. Under MCL 339.2512d(2)(g), has the listing agent violated the confidentiality duty?
choice_a: No, because real estate licensees are exempt from confidentiality duties toward each other
choice_b: No, as long as the information was true
choice_c: Yes, but only if the competing licensee then shares it with a buyer
choice_d: Yes, because the information was disclosed to a licensee who is not an agent of the client, without the client's permission and not as provided by law
explanation: Subsection (2)(g) specifically bars disclosure of confidential client information to any licensee who is not an agent of the client, absent client permission or a legal exception.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(3), the services listed in subsections (3)(a) through (e) are described using what kind of statutory language?
choice_a: Mandatory ('shall provide'), subject only to the limited waiver allowed for (3)(b), (c), and (d) under subsection (5)
choice_b: Purely discretionary ('may provide')
choice_c: Mandatory only for brokers, never for salespersons
choice_d: Mandatory only if the client is unrepresented by counsel
explanation: Subsection (3) opens with 'shall provide,' making the listed services mandatory except to the extent (3)(b), (c), and (d) are knowingly waived via a limited service agreement under subsection (5).

question: MCL 339.2512d separates a licensee's minimum obligations under a service provision agreement into two categories. What are they?
choice_a: Subsection (2) 'broker obligations' and subsection (3) 'salesperson obligations'
choice_b: Subsection (2) 'duties' (e.g., loyalty, confidentiality, accounting) and subsection (3) 'services' (e.g., marketing, offer presentation, closing assistance)
choice_c: Subsection (2) 'buyer obligations' and subsection (3) 'seller obligations'
choice_d: There is only one category; subsections (2) and (3) are identical restatements
explanation: Subsection (2) sets out fiduciary-type duties owed to the client, while subsection (3) sets out concrete services the licensee must perform.

question: Under MCL 339.2512g(1), how many of the listed conditions (a)-(d) must be present for a right-to-list home sale agreement to be void and unenforceable?
choice_a: All four conditions must be present simultaneously
choice_b: At least three of the four conditions
choice_c: Just one; the agreement is void if any of the listed conditions apply
choice_d: None; the list is merely illustrative and non-binding
explanation: Subsection (1) states the agreement is void and unenforceable 'if any of the following apply,' so a single violation is sufficient.

question: Under MCL 339.2512d(3)(e), when a broker or associate real estate broker is involved at closing, the closing statement furnished to buyer and seller must be signed by whom?
choice_a: The title insurance company only
choice_b: The buyer's attorney
choice_c: Any licensee present at closing, regardless of role
choice_d: The broker or associate real estate broker
explanation: Subsection (3)(e) requires the closing statement to be signed by the broker or associate real estate broker who is involved at closing.
